meta.title: Our Last Month
meta.textType: functional: a program with a key, and a leaflet

paragraphs: On Monday, March first, Teacher Kim gave every pupil a program sheet. Lily, Mia, Leo, and May sat at their desks. Each of them had a copy. "This is our program for the last month of Primary Six," said Teacher Kim. "March is a special month, because Friday, March nineteenth is our last day of school." At the bottom of the sheet, there was a box with a key of five small pictures. "Look at the key first," she said. "A pencil is for a test, a flag is for the Explorers, and a camera is for the trip." "A screen is for the video call, and a star is for Farewell Day."

The timetable shows every activity of the month in time order. Nurse Jill's talk is held on Thursday, March fourth, in the club hour. The three tests are held at nine o'clock in the morning. English is on Monday, math is on Tuesday, and science is on Wednesday. "Which day is the science test?" asked Leo. May found the pencil beside the word "Wednesday." "It is on Wednesday, March tenth," she said. The last trip of the Explorers is on Saturday, March thirteenth. The bus leaves the school gate at half past eight. The Explorers have a weekly meeting on Thursday. The last meeting is on Thursday, March eighteenth. "When is the video call?" asked Mia. "It is on Tuesday, March sixteenth, at half past four," said Teacher Kim. "In Singapore, it will be half past five." Farewell Day is the last event on the program. A star is printed beside it.

Next, Teacher Kim handed out a second sheet, a leaflet from the town sports center. Its title was "Holiday Fun for Young People." The leaflet gives information about four activities. There is a swimming course, a dancing class, rugby for beginners, and an advanced class on Saturdays. The sign-up day is printed at the bottom: Friday, March nineteenth. Lily circled it with a red pencil. Leo drew a small star beside "Dancing class" as a joke.

"Who can take part?" asked Leo. "Children from ten to fourteen years old can take part," said Teacher Kim. "The price of each course is printed on the back." "Places are available until Friday," she said. "The advanced class is for children who already know the sport," she added. "A star is for Farewell Day, not for dancing," said Mia. Leo grinned. "I may take part in the dancing class," he said. "One day, you may see me on a stage." "You might be very good at it," said May.
Lily put both sheets into her bag and looked at the program again. "Our last month will be busy," she said. "It will be fun, too," said Mia.
